description: About Etched Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across both prefill and decode workloads. Our first products are heavily focused on inference. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history. Job Summary We are seeking talented Spring ‘27 and Summer ‘27 IA Research Engineer interns to build the agents that accelerate how Etched produces frontier tokens. You will embed with our kernels team and work alongside our founders on agentic harnesses, tools, and evals that let agents do long-running engineering work people actually rely on. This role is for builders who thrive on ambiguity, have real product sense, and want to own problems end to end. Key responsibilities Embed with our kernels team to find high-leverage bottlenecks and help turn them into tools engineers use every day. Build and deploy LLM agents wired into our engineering workflows via tool-calling and MCP. Help build execution environments where agents can verify their own work, with sandboxed access to simulators, compilers, profilers, and real hardware. Ship internal products end to end, including the interfaces, data pipelines, and infrastructure behind them. Design evals and track adoption to measure which tools are working and which aren’t. Support special projects with the founders across the company. You may be a good fit if you have Progress towards a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a related field Strong software engineering fundamentals and a record of shipping projects other people use Built agents for multi-step tasks beyond calling an API: tool design, context management, evals, and failure analysis Heavy use of coding agents, including reading their transcripts and changing the system when an agent is confidently wrong High agency in unfamiliar domains, product sense, and extreme attention to detail Strong candidates may have some experience with Chip development, GPU kernels, hardware, or manufacturing Infrastructure, data engineering, or DevOps Fine-tuning, RAG over technical data, or multi-agent orchestration Hackathons, startups, or side projects with real users We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every qualification. Program details 12-week paid internship Generous housing support for those relocating Daily lunch and dinner in our office Based at our office in San Jose, CA Direct mentorship from industry leaders and world-class engineers Opportunity to work on one of the most important problems of our time For any questions, contact internships@etched.com. How we’re different Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors. We are a fully in-person team in San Jose (Santana Row), and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.

description: About us Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia. We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do. Our co-founders are Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor . Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace. Sierra’s Applied Research team works to make the models behind our agents better, faster, and cheaper across many kinds of tasks. Our work covers post-training open-weight models for specialized capabilities, new approaches to voice AI, and the benchmarks the field uses to measure agents, including τ-bench. As an Applied Research Intern, you’ll join the team for a research project, working with a mentor, you’ll pick a problem that matters to how AI agents perform in the real world, run rigorous experiments, and potentially write up what you find for a top venue. If you want your research to reach both the research community and production agents used by millions of people, come do it at Sierra. What you’ll do Own a research project from start to finish, from framing the question and running experiments to writing and submitting a paper. Push agent evaluation forward, for example by extending τ-bench to new domains, modalities, or long-horizon tasks, or by building new ways to measure reliability and consistency. Study how agents reason, use tools, and follow policies over multi-turn conversations, and find out where and why they fail. Explore post-training methods such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to improve agent behavior, and measure the gains rigorously. Work with large-scale, proprietary datasets of text and audio interactions to find research questions grounded in real customer problems. Work with researchers and engineers across Sierra, and where it makes sense, turn your findings into improvements in production. What you’ll bring Currently pursuing a PhD in computer science, machine learning, or a related field. A research track record, such as first-author publications or submissions at venues like NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, Interspeech or ICASSP. Strong experimental skills: you design clean experiments, build careful baselines, and are honest about what the results do and do not show. Fluency in Python and modern ML tooling (for example, PyTorch, and LLM inference and training stacks). High agency and a builder’s mindset. You’ll work across the stack to get an experiment running. Clear, direct communication, both in writing and when presenting research. Even better Research experience with LLM agents, tool use, or multi-turn dialogue. Experience designing benchmarks or evaluations, especially ones tied to real-world outcomes. Experience with supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or long-horizon optimization. Experience with speech, voice, or multimodal models. Open-source contributions to ML research code or benchmarks. Intern qualifications The internship is open to students currently enrolled in a PhD program. Duration and start dates are flexible. Interns are embedded with the Applied Research team and work under the guidance of a mentor. The internship is based in our San Francisco office. We are in person Monday through Thursday. Our values Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work. Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it. Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve. Intensity: We know we don’t have the luxury of patience. We play to win. We care about our product being the best, and when it isn’t, we fix it. When we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time. Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We are the best technology company for parents. We support and respect each other and celebrate each other’s personal and professional achievements. What we offer We want our benefits to reflect our values and offer the following to full-time employees: Flexible (unlimited) paid time off Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family Life insurance and disability benefits Retirement plan dependent on country of employment Parental leave Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot Lunch, as well as delicious snacks and coffee to keep you energized Discretionary

description: Company Overview ACS (Allen Control Systems) is a defense technology company building precision robotic systems for the United States and its allies. Founded by two former U.S. Navy electrical engineers with deep experience in robotics and software, ACS brings together AI, computer vision, precision motion, and advanced hardware to solve complex defense challenges across land, air, and maritime environments. Our flagship product, Bullfrog, is an autonomous precision weapon system that transforms existing weapons into highly accurate counter-drone systems — giving warfighters a scalable, cost-effective response to one of the fastest-growing threats on the modern battlefield. Bullfrog is deployed with U.S. forces, and ACS works with organizations throughout the U.S. military and national security community. Following a $200 million Series B at a $2.2 billion valuation, ACS is rapidly expanding manufacturing, accelerating Bullfrog deployments, and developing the next generation of autonomous battlefield systems. This is an opportunity to join a proven, fast-moving team and help scale technology with direct, real-world impact on national security. description: Wheeled Platforms & Lifting Systems Emeryville, California | Internship Proposed base compensation. Final terms are subject to Astera’s hiring process. About Astera Astera Institute is a private foundation supporting ambitious work in science and technology through grants, investments, and in-house research. Its research programs combine the pace and autonomy of a startup with the freedom to pursue difficult scientific questions. Learn more about Astera’s mission at astera.org/vision . About the Robotics Lab We are building a frontier robotics lab at Astera Institute. We believe neuroscience and AI will converge in embodied intelligence: animals and robots face shared challenges of perceiving their surroundings, navigating, manipulating objects, and using memory and reasoning to accomplish tasks in the physical world. Robotics provides a powerful testbed for investigating how biological neural circuits solve these challenges and for developing AI systems that turn perception, learning, and cognition into effective action. Our strategy starts with making robots useful, while developing a mechanistic understanding of how neural circuits can generate intelligent behavior. We aim to continually expand the repertoire of behaviors a robot can perform reliably in real environments, while improving its ability to learn new skills, adapt to changing conditions, and recover from failure. These practical capabilities provide both measurable outcomes and a foundation for investigating deeper principles of intelligence. Wheeled robotic platforms are one of the embodiments we use to test neural-circuit models and AI systems as we work toward general embodied intelligence. We have already demonstrated indoor navigation on a simple differential-drive platform. We are now expanding this work to evaluate other wheel and drivetrain configurations, along with lifting systems that allow robots to adjust their working height. Position Summary Help us build and compare the systems that allow robots to move and adjust their working height. Under engineering mentorship, you will prototype wheeled mobile bases and lifting platforms, run hands-on experiments, and evaluate how different designs perform under realistic operating conditions. Starting with our existing hoverboard hub motors and other motorized wheel hardware, you will help explore different wheel and drivetrain configurations. You will also help develop and evaluate lifting platforms, comparing commercially available mechanisms and custom prototypes. Your work will help the team select practical designs based on measured performance, reliability, cost, and ease of integration. Core Responsibilities Evaluate wheeled platforms. Assemble and modify mobile bases using hoverboard hub motors, hub motor wheels, and conventional motor-driven wheel assemblies. Help design and fabricate chassis, mounts, and supporting components. Compare navigation performance of different systems. Compare wheel and drivetrain configurations. Develop repeatable tests to evaluate maneuverability, low-speed motion, traction, payload handling, power consumption, steerability and general performance across relevant floor surfaces. Prototype lifting platforms. Help assemble, adapt, and test different lifting mechanisms, such as scissor lifts and telescoping lifting columns. Integrate actuators, guides, mounts, and supporting structures. Evaluate lifting performance. Compare lifting range, speed, positioning repeatability, rigidity, and stability under defined loads. Investigate vibration, mechanical play, and other issues that affect reliable operation. Integrate controls and measurements. Configure motor controllers, connect position and speed feedback, and develop simple control and data-collection scripts. Help implement travel limits, homing, and coordinated motion under engineering supervision. Document comparisons and improve designs. Maintain CAD files, wiring diagrams, parts lists, and test records. Summarize tradeoffs and work with engineers to refine promising designs. Keep experimental hardware ready. Organize components, tools, and spares; maintain prototypes and test fixtures; and assist with equipment inspections, repairs, and experiment setup. Required Qualifications Coursework, projects, or practical experience in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, robotics, mechatronics, or a related discipline. Experience building and troubleshooting a physical system through coursework, research, student teams, or personal projects. Basic familiarity with mechanical assembly, electrical wiring, motors, and sensors. Interest in hands-on prototyping and systematic testing, including careful measurement and documentation. Comfort working with an engineering mentor and contributing to the upkeep of a shared robotics lab. Preferred Experience CAD, 3D printing, machining, or fabrication of mechanical prototypes. BLDC motors, motor controllers, encoders, wheeled robots, or drivetrain design. Linear actuators, screw drives, scissor lifts, lifting columns, or other positioning mechanisms. Python, C/C++, microcontrollers, or basic feedback control. Building test fixtures, collecting experimental data, or comparing hardware designs. Prior experience with every technology listed is not expected. We value curiosity, practical problem-solving, and an interest in understanding how different mechanical systems perform through real experiments.

description: 🎨 OpusClip is the world's No.1 AI video agent, built for authenticity on social media. Within just 18 months of our launch, over 20 million creators and businesses have used OpusClip to enhance their social presence. About the Role OpusClip is hiring a CX Test Automation Intern: a software-developer-in-test who sits inside the Customer Experience team and turns real customer tickets into automated UI end-to-end tests. You will be the first person in a new lane we call customer-originated requirements: the thousands of support conversations we handle each month are a rich record of how OpusClip actually gets used and where it breaks, and nobody has yet turned that record into a repeatable test battery. This is a 4-month co-op based in Vancouver, starting January 7, 2027, with the option to extend for a further 8 months. The first 4 months hold a bounded, well-defined backlog that is valuable on its own; the extension is a decision we make together, not an assumption. You will work with AI coding tools (Claude Code, Codex) every day, ship real automation into a real product, and leave with a portfolio of tests that protect paying customers. CX at OpusClip is built as a talent nursery: people who start here move into data, engineering and customer-facing technical roles. This role is designed as one of those on-ramps. This role suits a student or early-career engineer who has already built and shipped something with AI assistance, likes finding the edge cases others miss, and cares about the people on the other side of the product as much as the code. Key Responsibilities Turn customer tickets into automated tests Your core output is a UI end-to-end test battery grounded in real customer reports. You will mine support conversations and bug tickets for the workflows customers actually run and the moments where they fail, reproduce those failures, and write automated tests that catch them before the next customer does. Each test traces back to a ticket, so the battery grows in the direction of real user pain rather than hypothetical coverage. Success here is measured by the share of customer-reported regressions your tests would have caught, and by how much faster CX can confirm a reported issue is real. Map user workflows into testable moments Before a test exists, someone has to break a workflow like "upload a video, get clips, export to TikTok" into its discrete steps, decision points and failure modes, and rank them by how many customers they touch. You will do this mapping with the CX team, who hold the ticket data, and document it so that Product and Engineering can reuse it. Over time this becomes a living map of how OpusClip is used, maintained from the customer side. Work AI-native You will build with Claude Code or Codex as your primary tool: scoping a task, giving the model the right context, breaking the work into steps, reviewing and iterating on the output, and knowing when the first answer is wrong. You will also help the CX team adopt the same habits, sharing patterns and small tools that let non-engineers verify issues and query data on their own. Bridge CX and Engineering You sit in CX but your work lands in Engineering's repositories and CI. You will open pull requests, respond to code review, follow branch and merge conventions, and report flaky or failing tests with clear reproduction steps. When a test exposes a product gap, you will write it up with the customer context, the business impact and a proposed priority, so that the people who own the fix can act on it without a second round of questions. Qualifications and Requirements Hands-on vibe coding experience: Must-have. You have built and shipped something real with AI assistance (a side project, internal tool or script) and can walk through how it was built: what you asked for, what the model got wrong, and how you fixed it. Can read Python and JavaScript/TypeScript: Must-have. You can explain what a short snippet does and spot an obvious bug. You do not need to write either language from scratch. Testing mindset: Must-have. Given a feature such as "upload a video, get clips", you list the happy path, edge cases and failure modes, then rank them by user impact rather than by how easy they are to test. Customer empathy: Must-have. You want to understand what the user was trying to do, not just what broke. You read a ticket and see a person with a deadline, not a bug ID. Clear communication and cross-functional collaboration: Must-have. Your write-ups are short, specific and readable by someone who was not in the room. You ask for review and take feedback without friction. Grasp of business impact: Must-have. You can reason about ROI and opportunity cost: why fixing a bug that hits 2% of paying exports beats one that hits a rarely used free feature, and what it costs to test the wrong thing. Breaks user workflows into discrete moments: Must-have. You can take "upload a video, get clips, post to TikTok" and name each step, each decision the user makes and each place it can go wrong. Curiosity or background in video editing and media: Nice-to-have. You have made, edited or published vid

At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done. Snowflake started as the place companies go to understand their data. Now we're making it the place where AI agents put that data to work: investigating business questions, testing explanations and recommending what to do next, all within the rules people set. The Agentic Analytics Product Marketing team sits at the center of that shift, taking products like Cortex Agents, Cortex Analyst, semantic views and interactive warehouses to market. description: About Taara: Born at X, Google's Moonshot Factory, Taara is on a mission to connect billions of people lacking abundant and affordable internet today by pioneering the way we use light to deliver faster, cheaper, more reliable connectivity. We are bringing groundbreaking wireless optical communication and photonics chip technologies to the world to bridge the digital divide. Joining Taara allows you to work as part of a multidisciplinary team of experts in optics, software, and hardware, all collaborating to solve the hardest connectivity challenges on a global scale. If you want to tackle problems that matter and build tools with real-world impact, we would love to meet you. About the Role: As an Optical PLL Research Intern , you will lay the groundwork for an integrated optical phase-locked loop (OPLL) that locks an external laser for coherent reception in next-generation wireless optical links. This is a long-term project spanning lab and simulation, ideally a year or more. It could also anchor a thesis or a longer-term collaboration. What such a loop can achieve is bounded by real components. You will evaluate lasers, modulators, and analog electronics, build benchtop experiments around them, and work toward a stable closed loop. In parallel, you will extend our simulation and use the two to check each other. There is genuine room to shape the direction. Survey what is available, design your own experiments, and follow the evidence to the strongest design. How you will make 10X Impact: Component Evaluation: Screen commercial lasers, modulators, and photodetectors. Measure what vendors do not publish. Loop Design: Design the loops that track carrier phase and frequency, and validate them against control theory. Chip Requirements: Define what the integrated OPLL needs from its laser, electronics, and loop. Physical-Layer Simulation: Extend our model of the link and reconcile it with measurement. What you should have: Currently pursuing a Master's or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, Optics, Communications, or a related field. A strong background in analog and RF electronics and circuit design , including noise, bandwidth, and delay analysis. Hands-on lab experience with lasers, modulators, photodetectors , and high-speed test equipment. Control theory applied on hardware: closing feedback loops and diagnosing oscillation, drift, or loss of lock. Working knowledge of digital communications and signal processing . Availability of at least 6 months, ideally 12 or more, and three days per week in the Sunnyvale office. It'd be great if you also had one or more of these: Laser Locking: Frequency stabilization, tunable sources, phase-locked loops, carrier recovery, or coherent detection. Photodetection & Front-End Electronics: Photoreceiver, TIA, or high-speed circuit design. Numerical Methods: Scientific Python (NumPy, SciPy, JAX), phase-noise modeling, or cycle-slip statistics. Domain Knowledge: Optical or RF communications, photonics, or fading channels. What we offer: Competitive salary: $7,000–$10,000/month depending on degree. Flexible duration to fit your academic schedule. Direct mentorship from industry-leading engineers in a "moonshot" environment. Opportunity to work on technology that has the potential to change how billions of people access the internet.

description: At Upvest, we are on a mission to make investing as easy as spending money . Upvest empowers businesses to offer a wide range of investment products and the best experience in the field of capital market investment and retirement planning. Upvest’s Investment API is easy to integrate so that fintechs and financial institutions can save resources and fully focus on their core business. We are proud to partner with Europe’s leading Fintechs and financial institutions such as DKB, Revolut, N26 and Raisin. Founded in 2017 by Martin Kassing, Upvest now brings together over 270 talented professionals from more than 70 nationalities. Upvest is backed by €280M in total funding from world-class investors, including BlackRock, Tencent, Sapphire Ventures, and Bessemer Venture Partners, Earlybird, Notion Capital, and Motive . Our latest €105M funding round in March 2026 - led by Sapphire and Tencent - serves as a massive catalyst for our growth, allowing us to offer premier investment experience. About the role: Germany's private pension system is being rebuilt from the ground up. From 1 January 2027, the Altersvorsorgedepot (AVD) replaces the Riester-Rente as the country's state-subsidised private pension and Upvest is building the operational infrastructure that lets fintechs and banks offer it to millions of savers. Join us as a Working Student in Client Experience and you'll be there before Day 1: helping design the processes, then running them once they go live. This is a rare chance to see a regulated financial product being built from a blank page, rather than inheriting one that already works. What you’ll do: Support our clients: Our partners' support teams field questions from their end-users about subsidies, transfers and payouts. You'll help prepare clear, accurate answers and learn to translate dense regulation into language a customer can act on. Support day-to-day AVD operations: Help run the core processes that keep the product working, e.g. contract registration with the ZfA (Zentrale Zulagenstelle für Altersvermögen), contribution management, the annual bonus application (AZ01), and payment reconciliation. You'll learn how a state-subsidised pension product actually functions behind the interface. Help build the playbooks: As we prepare for launch, we're writing the processes from scratch. You'll help document workflows, build step-by-step guides and error catalogues, and keep them current as the rules and our systems evolve; the foundations the team will scale on. Support error handling and reconciliation: Work through recurring error cases from the ZfA, check that payments and records match, and help spot the patterns behind repeat issues so they can be fixed at the root rather than one at a time. Spot what should be better: You'll see every manual workaround first-hand. We want your view on what's slow, error-prone, or worth automating; and you'll have the room to say so. What you bring: Fluent German communication skills (B2/C1), along with comfortable working proficiency in English This one is a hard requirement rather than a nice-to-have: the regulation, the correspondence with the ZfA, and most of the documentation you'll work with day to day are all in German. You're structured and genuinely precise. In this role, small details carry real consequences for someone's pension, and you're the kind of person who notices when a number doesn't add up. You're curious about rules rather than put off by them. You're willing to read the actual regulation to understand why a process works the way it does. You're comfortable with ambiguity. The product is brand new, so some answers don't exist yet; you'll ask good questions instead of waiting for perfect instructions. You're confident with spreadsheets and AI tooling. Any prior exposure to financial services, operations or a regulated environment is a bonus, but not required. You're available for a minimum of 6 months and based in Berlin. How we Upvest in you: Impact-driven work: We’re building the infrastructure that will power the future of investing in Europe. It’s complex, ambitious, and meaningful. You’ll work with modern technologies and create something entirely new. No legacy systems, no limits. Team celebrations: Participate in company-wide events, such as UpFest, dinners, offsites and our Holiday party, to connect with colleagues and celebrate our achievements. Inclusion : We’re committed to a culture where everyone belongs and thrives. Our Employee Resources Groups foster inclusion and connection, like Upfem for our female Upvengers, or UpVergent supporting neurodivergent Upvengers and allies. Our Values: Make it easy for others. The ACLU seeks a Legal Intern in the National Political Advocacy Department of the ACLU’s National office in Washington, DC. This internship is part-time and hybrid.

Qualifying applicants must currently be matriculated undergraduate students or an equivalent combination of education and/or experience and must be based in the U.S. for the entire duration of the internship.

 

The Team:

The National Political Advocacy Department (NPAD) works to strengthen the efforts of the ACLU at the federal, state, and local levels of government. The department harnesses the political power that comes from having more than eight million members and supporters, as well as affiliates in every state. By organizing grassroots lobbying and issue campaigns using modern tactics, the ACLU seeks to continue to achieve change as profound in the legislative, administrative and electoral arenas as it accomplishes through the courts.  

The Democracy and Technology Policy & Government Affairs team is made up of eight members, including seven attorneys, who work with Congress, state legislatures, regulatory agencies and others to strengthen and protect rights to voting, free speech, and privacy; to advance racial justice; and to ensure that emerging technologies (in artificial intelligence, algorithmic decision-making, and surveillance) are not used to deny rights or discriminate.

What You’ll Do:

The intern will work on legal and policy research and writing-related projects centered on voting, racial justice, free speech, technology policy, or democracy reform. They will assist members of our team with researching and analyzing legislation, elected officials, coalition partners, and relevant developments in the political and advocacy landscapes on the state and federal levels. They will help prepare advocacy and public education materials, correspondence, and reports as needed. They will also support our team's efforts to do congressional outreach through the form of briefings, meetings on Capitol Hill, and letters.

Your Day to Day

description:
What we’re building

The marine industry supports recreation, global commerce, and national defense. And yet it runs on technology that hasn't meaningfully changed in fifty years. Until now.

Arc is on a mission to electrify the marine industry. We're rethinking powertrains, software, and vessel designs from first principles. And we're already executing. We started with consumers to develop and harden our core technology. We’re now scaling production of our flagship model with new models and sectors on the horizon. Now we’re extending our platform to commercial applications, starting with tugs, ferries, and defense, with years worth of signed contracts and a pipeline that spans every vessel type on the water.

The technology is proven, the momentum is building, and the opportunity is enormous. The marine industry is going electric and Arc is building the platform that powers it

Who we’re looking for

We’re looking for a curious, hands-on engineer who wants to understand how things are built and make the process better. You’ll join our Manufacturing Engineering team in Torrance, working alongside engineers, technicians, supervisors, and quality partners on real production challenges.

With mentorship from a full-time engineer, you’ll own a scoped improvement project from observing the process and collecting data through implementing a solution and measuring the results. You should enjoy spending time on the production floor, listening to the people doing the work, and turning ideas into practical improvements.

Internship Term - June 14–August 20, 2027, onsite at our Torrance headquarters.

What You'll Do

  • Observe production processes and perform time studies to identify bottlenecks, excess motion, rework, and opportunities to reduce build hours.
  • Create and improve work instructions, process flows, and assembly sequences with input from technicians and engineers.
  • Design, prototype, and validate tools, fixtures, and shop aids that improve repeatability, ergonomics, and build quality.
  • Support root-cause investigations into production issues and help implement corrective actions.
  • Partner with design engineering and quality to improve manufacturability and support the introduction of new parts or processes.
  • Use build and quality data to compare performance before and after changes, documenting results and lessons learned.
  • Present your project, results, and recommended next steps to the team at the end of the internship.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Pursuing a degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical or a related engineering discipline.
  • Experience building, assembling, testing, or improving hardware through coursework, a student team, research, an internship, or personal projects.
  • Foundational understanding of engineering drawings, tolerances, and common manufacturing or assembly methods.
  • Basic ability to create or modify parts in a 3D CAD tool.
  • Ability to organize and analyze data using Excel, Google Sheets, or a similar tool.
  • Clear communication, attention to detail, and a collaborative approach to solving problems.
  • Willingness to work hands-on in a production environment, follow safety procedures, and learn from technicians.

Bonus Qualifications

  • Experience with composites, bonding, trimming, finishing, mechanical assembly, or battery manufacturing.
  • Exposure to time studies, standard work, line balancing, lean manufacturing, or continuous improvement.
  • Experience designing fixtures or using machining, 3D printing, or other fabrication methods.
  • Familiarity with NX, Teamcenter, a manufacturing execution system, or digital work instructions.
  • Experience on a student engineering team or in a manufacturing setting.
  • Interest in electric vehicles, boats, and improving how products are built.

At Arc, we encourage diversity and consider all qualified applicants equally for employment, regardless of background, identity, or status. You’re always welcome to reach out even if you don’t meet many of these qualifications. Passion and aptitude make up for a lot.

What we offer

The base pay for this role is $36 per hour. 

Additionally, as an Arc Intern, you'll also get:

  • Boat days – Yes, we actually go out on the water. A lot.
  • Retirement savings — Traditional and Roth 401(k) access
  • Safety support — Reimbursement for PPE, ergonomic equipment, and anything that ensures we keep our crew safe
  • Relocation Assistance
  • Mentorship Opportunities
  • Office perks — Daily lunches, snacks, and good coffee while onsite

Our values

We move with urgency and build with care. We value these five things above all else:

  • Ownership over both your work and the company’s success
  • Empathy for colleagues and for customers
  • Humility in problem solving and collaboration
  • Pragmatism for navigating ambiguity quickly and sensibly 
  • Inclusion of different backgrounds, opinions, cultures, and perspectives.

We want people who share and embody these values. It is vital that our values align - we’d be happy to elaborate on any or all of these during the interview process.

description:
Astranis builds advanced satellites for high orbits, expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. Today Astranis satellites provide dedicated, secure networks to highly-sophisticated customers across the globe – large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military. 

With five satellites on orbit and many more set to launch soon, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization.

Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Baillie Gifford, Blackrock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA.

Procurement Intern (Winter 2027)

Internships at Astranis typically last for twelve weeks and are hourly roles designed for students who are currently enrolled at a four-year university.

As an Intern, you will have an amazing opportunity to work on hard problems. We pride ourselves on giving everyone at Astranis a chance to do meaningful work on challenging projects, no matter their seniority. Many past interns have designed, built, and tested flight hardware and software heading to space on our satellites, and many of them are now full-time employees at Astranis. (If you have already graduated from a four-year university or are enrolled in a graduate program, please apply to be an Associate.)

Role

  • Work with and support the Supply Chain product team at Astranis, in San Francisco
  • Assist with RFQs, POs, and data integrity within all systems while ensuring all commercial terms are agreed and documented
  • Establish and manage ongoing, sustainable processes to help our company scale
  • Provide operational support for our spacecraft and technology development programs as needed

Requirements

  • Comfortable working in a busy, ever-changing environment and helping bring order to chaos
  • Strong reasoning and analytical abilities
  • Extremely organized and detail-oriented
  • Ability to handle multiple tasks at once and prioritize accordingly
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills 
The base pay for this position is $29.00 per hour.
Base Hourly Pay
$29—$29 USD
U.S. Citizenship, Lawful Permanent Residency, or Refugee/Asylee Status Required
(To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States, or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3))
 
Our mission and products are built for everyone, regardless of gender, race, creed, or background. We believe in a diverse and inclusive workplace, and we invite all people to join our team and bring their unique perspectives to make us stronger.

description:
A Rare Opportunity to Shape the Future of Genomics

Join a team of brilliant, passionate innovators determined to transform healthcare. At BillionToOne, we've built a category-defining, publicly traded company on Nasdaq where transparency fuels trust, collaboration drives breakthroughs, and every contribution moves the needle on our mission to make life-changing diagnostics accessible to all. We don't just aim for incremental improvements; we build products that are 10x better than anything that exists today.

Our scientists, engineers, sales executives, and visionaries are united by an unwavering commitment to changing the standard of care in prenatal and cancer diagnostics. This is where cutting-edge science meets human compassion, and every innovation you contribute helps remove the fear of the unknown from some of life's most critical medical moments.

If you're driven by purpose, energized by innovation, and ready to help shape the future of precision medicine at scale, this is where you belong.

The Research Associate Intern position at BillionToOne is exceptionally rare at the undergraduate or early-career level. At BillionToOne, you will do much more than simply run routine protocols. Your work will shape the development of high-impact molecular diagnostic products that are actively changing patient outcomes in both oncology and prenatal medicine. This is your chance to contribute to building novel molecular tests that help patients from day one.

You will work alongside and be mentored by scientists with interdisciplinary expertise across molecular biology, genomics, bioinformatics, and quantitative modeling. You will have the chance to use cutting-edge molecular techniques, next-generation sequencing, and robotic tools to move assays from research prototypes to commercially available products run at large scale on real patient samples in our clinical lab. Whether your ambition is to grow here at BillionToOne or ultimately pursue graduate studies, this position would be a solid foundation for your scientific career.

The Research Associate intern is an on-site position in our Menlo Park, CA office.

Candidates who expect to graduate before Fall 2027 or who have already graduated are encouraged to apply to our full-time Research Associate position.

Who We’re Looking For:

  • Strong statistical and quantitative skills: You think rigorously about data. You understand the difference between signal and noise, appreciate the importance of statistical power, and bring quantitative reasoning to every problem.
  • Meticulous attention to experimental detail: You understand that the quality of an experiment determines what we can learn from it. You keep rigorous records, design careful controls, and take pride in work that others can rely on and build upon.
  • Ambition to make a difference now: You aren’t here to punch the clock. You want to understand why things work, push the boundaries of what’s known, and do what it takes to see your contributions show up in products that help real patients.
  • Excellent communication in a fast-paced, collaborative environment: We move quickly and we move together. You share findings clearly and proactively, ask questions early rather than late, and work seamlessly across scientists, engineers, and cross-functional teams to keep projects moving.

Responsibilities:

  • Design, execute, and troubleshoot experiments and assays under the guidance of Senior Scientists
  • Learn analytical and computational methodologies to analyze results under the guidance of Senior Scientists
  • Present scientific findings both verbally at group meetings and via internal written reports
  • Document experimental details and results

Qualifications:

  • Must be enrolled in an undergraduate or master’s degree program during Fall 2027
  • Anticipated BS or MS in Bioengineering, Molecular and Cell Biology, Microbiology, Biophysics, Biochemistry, or related field
  • Independent research experience
  • An ability to quickly learn mathematical, analytical, and experimental concepts
  • High mathematical and statistical aptitude (e.g., you find GRE math section to be extremely easy)
  • Great attention to detail

Nice-To-Haves:

  • Experience with standard molecular biology techniques relating to DNA such as PCR
  • Experience in a cell-free DNA setting
  • Experience with next-generation sequencing library preparation
  • Experience with computational analysis in R, Python, or other programming language

Benefits And Perks:

  • Working with a team of ‘rockstars’ who bring out the best in everyone
  • Open, transparent culture that includes weekly Town Hall meetings
  • The ability to indirectly or directly change the lives of hundreds of thousand patients
  • Free daily on-site lunches provided from top eateries
  • Latest and greatest hardware (laptop, lab equipment, facilities)
  • A variety of perks on campus (state of the art gym, restaurant)
  • Free on-site EV charging (compatible with all EVs, including Tesla)

At BillionToOne, we are proud to offer a combination of (1) competitive base pay, and (2) the opportunity for professional growth.

For this position, the base pay rate is $25 per hour.

description:
The Company You’ll Join

Carta is the connected platform and AI-native ecosystem for private capital. Built to replace fragmented tools with a single system of record, Carta brings together the software, services, and legal infrastructure that founders use to manage equity, fund managers use to run administration and reporting, and legal teams use to close transactions. Trusted by 55,000 companies and 1.8M+ equity holders in 160+ countries, and 10,000 funds and SPVs representing $250B+ in assets under management, Carta is transforming how private capital operates. Recognized by Fortune, Forbes, Fast Company, Inc. and Great Places to Work.

For more information about our offices and culture, check out our Carta careers page.

The Team You'll Work With

Carta is looking for a Marketing Intern to join our Singapore team between January to June 2027.

Carta opened its Singapore office in 2021, and since then, has been building a world-class team to support the startup and investor ecosystem across Asia Pacific, the Middle East and Africa. 

The Marketing Intern will report up to Carta’s Head of Marketing for APAC & MEA, and get the chance to work firsthand on a range of projects, including marketing campaigns, website optimization, marketing analytics, event support and more. This role will give you the opportunity to try out the different realms of marketing and gain the necessary skill sets to jumpstart your career in B2B tech.

The Problem You'll Solve

  • Campaigns: Work with the demand generation leads to launch campaigns across the region, and A/B test and optimize lead generation efforts across online and offline channels
  • Content & PR: Partner with the regional team to localize blog articles to the region, edit bylines, craft organic social media content and develop customer case studies to increase brand awareness
  • Events: Support on digital & physical marketing collateral ideation and design (presentation decks, swag) as well as provide on-the-ground support for Virtual Events & physical events
  • Other ad-hoc tasks as assigned

The Impact You will Have

As a Marketing Intern at Carta, you will be an integral part of growing the marketing function in this region. You will drive demand in the market and help oversee Carta’s growth in APAC & MEA.

About You

  • Studying Bachelors Degree in a relevant field (business, marketing)
  • Previous internship or work experience in marketing would be preferred
  • Desire to learn and work in a fast-paced environment
  • Excellent time management and organizational skills
  • Interest in B2B Marketing as well as the startup space

Nice to have:

  • Experience with marketing and sales platforms (such as Salesforce, Marketo, Figma, Google Analytics, Google Ads, LinkedIn Ads)
  • Proficiencies with Microsoft Office and/or Google Suite (GSuite)
  • Knowledge of the startup and venture capital ecosystem

 

At Carta, you’re not just an employee. You’re a builder who is creating  infrastructure that accelerates innovation and empowers more ownership. Cartans are helpful, relentless, unconventional and kind; representing Carta’s Identity Traits. They work collaboratively and cross functionally  to challenge the status quo; working towards a common goal of creating more owners in the private markets. 

 

Disclosures:

  • We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to providing a positive interview experience for every candidate. If accommodations due to a disability or medical condition are needed, please connect with the talent partner via email. 
  • Carta uses E-Verify in the United States for employment authorization. See the E-Verify and Department of Justice websites for more details.
  • For information on our data privacy policies, see Privacy, CA Candidate Privacy, and Brazil Transparency Report.
  • Please note that all official communications from us will come from an @carta.com or @carta-external.com domain. Report any contact from unapproved domains to security@carta.com.

description:
Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model — which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.

The Team:

Our Value Engineers (VE) are the trusted advisors for the end-to-end customer value journey, and work on the intersection of technology and business. Value Engineers partner with sales and customers to create compelling solutions and prototypes within the Celonis software to critical business problems. A great VE understands the customer, the technology, and the sales cycle making it what may be the most interesting, challenging, and fulfilling role in enterprise technology sales.

The Role:

As a Strategic Program Management Intern within the Max Success Team you will support the steering of programs that implement/execute strategic decisions from our executive management into practice. These programs span across multiple organizations, centered in Value Engineering, spanning to Product, Strategy & Ops, Ecosystem, Services, Business Apps and others. You will ensure a program’s success by building up the strategic decisions.

The work you’ll do:

  • Enable and shape data driven decision making for our management and leverage Celonis AI capabilities.
  • Design and conceptualize strategic programs (incl. data analysis).
  • Support and oversee program execution from inception to completion.
  • Coordinate and guide all involved parties in their respective streams.
  • Take ownership of specific streams, ensuring their success.
  • Identify and mitigate potential risks to ensure smooth program delivery.
  • Report to our executive management on program progress and outcomes.

The qualifications you need:

  • Student of Business Administration / Industrial Engineering / Technology & Management / Economics / or of a comparable program
  • Ability to act autonomously in high ambiguity situations
  • Stakeholder management skills
  • Project management skills
  • Financial modeling in Google Sheets
  • Confidence to present to C-level executives and larger audiences
  • Experience in consulting and highly interested in data analytics
  • Passion for technology, data, OpenAI and LLMs and the impact it can have on the world
  • This internship can be done from our Madrid Office or Munich Office. Madrid is preferred.
  • Full-time availability for at least five months starting from December/ January 26/27

What Celonis can offer you:

  • Pioneer Innovation: Work with the global leader in Process Mining and the Process Intelligence Graph to shape the future of AI-driven business operations.
  • Ownership from Day 1: Every full-time "Celonaut" is an owner, receiving Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) and merit-based refresh grants.
  • Unrivaled Family Support: Benefit from our inclusive parental leave policy—24 weeks of fully paid leave for primary carers and 12 weeks for supporting carers, available from your first day of employment.
  • Work-Life Integration: Enjoy Unlimited PTO (in applicable regions) and generous PTO globally, as well as a flexible hybrid work model that balances remote focus with vibrant office collaboration.
  • Continuous Growth: Elevate your skills through our 70-20-10 learning framework, mentorship programs, and access to a dedicated learning platform.
  • Holistic Well-being: Prioritize your health with subsidized Wellhub memberships, mental health counseling, and dedicated "Wellness Weeks" that prioritize work/life balance.
  • Drive Sustainability: Participate in annual Impact Days, where you receive paid time off to volunteer for community and environmental causes with your local office, or virtually.
  • Global Inclusion & Belonging: Find community through our Inclusion Think Tank and participate in our annual Inclusion Days, ensuring every voice is heard and valued.
  • Value-Driven Impact: Join a mission-led organization where our core values—Live for Customer Value, The Best Team Wins, We Own It, and Earth Is Our Future—drive every decision.

description:
DB E.C.O. North America (with “E.C.O.” representing “Engineering, Consulting and Operations") offers specialized rail and transit consultancy services to public agencies, passenger and freight railroads. DB E.C.O. North America is part of the DB E.C.O. Group and leverages Deutsche Bahn’s global expertise to advance mobility and rail transportation across the U.S. and Canada. Their cross-disciplinary team collaborates closely with clients to innovate their portfolios and elevate business performance. With a focus on sustainability, safety, and operational excellence, they strive to enhance the customer experience, increase rail usage, and “Transform The Future Of Mobility.” 

Department: Consulting

Reports to: Manager

Location: Chicago, IL

Duration: June 2027 to August 2027

Schedule: 40 hours per week (in-person)

 

Application Deadline: Submit your resume and a short cover letter to the job posting by 5pm PT on November 13th, 2026. 

 

Tasks & Responsibilities:

You will work in one of the following portfolios of DB E.C.O. North America. Tell us your preferred portfolio in your cover letter.

  • Conceptual Rail Service, Operations, and Infrastructure Planning:
    • DB E.C.O. performs conceptual planning for public agencies, operators, and Class I railroads to design public transportation service plans, operation plans, and to identify effective infrastructure investments. We work across the full range of planning horizons from short-term projects for immediate implementation to long-term visioning projects. DB E.C.O. uses state-of-the-art methods and tools.
    • You will contribute to ongoing projects under the supervision of an experienced consultant and receive training in our methods and tools. Typical tasks:
      • Build and check timetable, ridership, and capacity datasets in Excel or Python
      • Support rail operations simulation and service plan development
      • Prepare GIS maps and other graphics for reports and client materials
      • Research peer systems and summarize findings for client deliverables
  • Governance and Integration Consulting:
    • DB E.C.O. consults public agencies to improve integration of the customer interface for public transportation systems and to facilitate cross-agency coordination. We draw on our expertise as the major operator of Germany’s integrated public transportation system to identify and adapt solutions for use in the U.S.
    • You will contribute to ongoing projects under the supervision of a manager and receive training in our methods and tools. Typical tasks:
      • Research German and European practices in fare integration, customer information, and agency coordination
      • Adapt those practices to U.S. agency and regulatory settings
      • Draft memos, slides, and graphics for client meetings

Requirements:

  • Working towards a degree in Civil Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Computer Science, or Transportation Planning (MS or equivalent)
  • Strong ability to think analytically and stay focused on developing solutions to complex technical matters
  • Demonstrable project or research experience
  • Organized, flexible, and able to work independently
  • Proficiency with MS Office suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
  • Professional fluency in English

Preferred:

  • Research or work experience in strategic rail planning, operations planning, or route management
  • Python, R, or GIS (ArcGIS or QGIS)
  • Exposure to rail simulation or scheduling software
  • German language skills (helpful for the Governance

AI and ML at Flagship Pioneering:
Flagship Pioneering is a scientific innovation engine that invents and builds companies that change the world. We bring entrepreneurial scientists together with experienced company builders and assemble the capital to allow them to take courageous leaps in human health, sustainability, technology and beyond. Artificial intelligence is core to how Flagship conceives and builds companies. We call our approach polyintelligence: human creativity and nature’s intelligence integrating and coexisting with artificial intelligence. This model runs across our ecosystem, where teams pair advances in AI and machine learning with foundational science to move from idea to concept faster and build AI-native companies that were previously out of reach.

Who we are looking for:
Computational scientists and engineers with broad interests and experience applying deep technical experience to out of distribution scientific questions. Standalone implementation isn’t the goal, it is creatively spotting opportunities where extension, modification and combination of bleeding edge computational and technical approaches can unlock new capabilities to solve consequential problems. Strong candidates will combine software engineering fundamentals with a readiness to embrace agentic development tools/practices and have experience implementing machine learning models and workflows across multiple model classes or scientific domains.

The Experience:
You will collaborate with Flagship Origination Teams and fellow ML scientists/engineers to explore what is made possible by big leaps beyond the current capabilities of AI. You will begin by asking ‘What if’ across a variety of ideas and building a ‘future backwards’ case for what needs to be true for them to become a reality. You will explore the tradeoffs across multiple options, including what and how much data is needed and where it might come from. You will work towards implementation and evaluation plans that enable us to address the real uncertainties, not just what is easy to measure.
With a project defined, you will begin to implement, evaluate and iterate. You will leverage Flagship's scalable GPU compute resources, data from our ecosystem, and the extensive expertise available across our teams.  You will implement the benchmarking capabilities needed to measure what matters and evaluate your designs. We will learn along the way and be ready to pivot on methods. Final work products are never just a model or a paper, they are wholistic answers to the future backwards questions we ask ourselves when originating the next big leap company.

The pay range for this role is $7,000 - $9,000 per month. This role is a short-term engagement that is not eligible for health and welfare benefits. Hive Financial Systems is an Atlanta-based fintech that builds and operates the technology behind responsible consumer lending for underserved borrowers. Our platform runs the full loan lifecycle (application, underwriting, servicing, payments, and collections) across multiple lending portfolios, and we are rebuilding it as a modern, cloud-native platform designed to scale.

Role Overview

We’re seeking a Software Engineering Intern to help build and modernize the platform behind our lending products: the services, APIs, data, and applications that borrowers and our internal teams rely on every day. You’ll join a product team working on our platform rebuild and ship real code alongside engineers, product managers, QA, and data specialists, with a mentor guiding you throughout the summer.

Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain features across our platform, primarily in C#/.NET services and APIs.
  • Write tests alongside your code. Our teams work test-first, so you’ll learn to write unit, integration, and end-to-end tests as part of every feature.
  • Help modernize legacy code into our new cloud-native platform, using AI-assisted tools to refactor and re-platform existing systems.
  • Work in short development cycles with code reviews, automated build pipelines, and feature flags.
  • Use AI tools responsibly in your daily work, and verify what they produce.
  • Collaborate with product, QA, data, and compliance partners. In lending, accuracy, security, and auditability are requirements, not extras.
  • Document what you build and share technical learnings with the team.

What You’ll Gain

  • Production experience on a platform used by real consumers and internal teams.
  • Hands-on work with a modern stack: C#/.NET, SQL, REST/GraphQL APIs, containers, and Microsoft Azure.
  • Experience with test-driven development, CI/CD, and cloud deployment.
  • An understanding of how engineering works in a regulated industry, including security, data privacy, and audit requirements.
  • An inside look at how fintech works end to end, from loan application to final payment.
  • A portfolio-ready project that demonstrates your contributions.

Qualifications

  • Current student pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field (rising Junior or Senior).
  • Programming experience in at least one object-oriented language; C# is preferred since our services are built on .NET.
  • Familiarity with SQL and relational databases.
  • Basic understanding of APIs and how services communicate with each other.
  • Hands-on experience using AI tools such as Claude, Cursor, Hex, and ChatGPT in coursework or projects, along with the judgment to review, test, and verify what AI produces.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, curiosity, and eagerness to learn.

Preferred Skills

  • Exposure to Python, TypeScript, or JavaScript.
  • Experience writing automated tests (for example, xUnit, NUnit, or pytest).
  • Familiarity with Git, cloud platforms (Azure preferred), or containers (Docker, Kubernetes).
  • Experience with Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, or Hex, which our team uses day to day, or with other agentic coding and AI-assisted analytics tools.
  • Familiarity with prompting, giving AI tools project context, or building small apps on top of an AI model’s API.

Interview Process

Our interview process includes multiple stages, starting with an initial screening. Candidates who advance will complete a technical assessment (TestGorilla) focused on coding and problem-solving. This helps ensure fairness and gives us a clear view of your technical capabilities.

Completing the TestGorilla assessment is required. Candidates who do not complete it will not move forward in the process.

description:
Actuarial internship for summer of 2027.

Horace Mann Educators Corporation offers insurance and financial products to educators and those who serve the public. We’re motivated by the fact that educators take care of our children’s future, and we believe they deserve someone to look after theirs. We help educators identify their financial goals and develop plans to achieve them. Our tailored offerings include special rates and benefits for educators, as well as the insurance we’re known for in order to help protect what they have today and the financial products to help prepare them for their futures. 

The Role

Our Property & Casualty (P&C) Actuarial team is seeking a P&C Actuarial Intern, who will focus on data analysis and contributions to projects throughout the department. In this role, the intern will deliver on a variety of projects and initiatives that help to measure and drive action around Actuarial department projects and initiatives. This intern will also gain exposure to financial modeling, risk assessment, and regulatory compliance within the insurance industry. It's a great opportunity to apply your quantitative skills and learn how actuarial principles are applied in real-world scenarios. Under direct supervision from various senior members of the team, you’ll also be conducting analyses that adhere to actuarial standards of practice: selecting appropriate data sources and methods, making necessary assumptions, recognizing considerations, and developing recommendations

The Day-to-Day

  • You'll work with large datasets to analyze insurance claims, policyholder information, and other relevant data.
  • Using statistical software like Excel or R, you’ll put your expertise to use to clean, organize, and analyze data sets.
  • Actively participate in various department and project-focused meetings, engage and contribute ideas, and gain exposure to cross-functional collaboration.
  • Learn to assess risks associated with insurance policies and understand how to price them accordingly.
  • Support your fellow Actuaries in various tasks such as calculating insurance premiums, determining reserves, and assessing risk levels for different insurance products.
  • Gain an understanding of the various insurance products offered by Horace Mann and their specific actuarial considerations
  • At times, you’ll assist in developing and updating financial models that predict future trends in insurance claims and financial outcomes to understand the impact of different variables.
  • Develop a comprehensive perspective of the field by shadowing seasoned actuaries, participating in industry events and webinars, and connecting with professionals at Horace Mann. 

Role Requirements

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in actuarial science, finance, economics, statistics, mathematics, business, or related field.
  • A minimum of one (1) Actuarial exam through either the Society of Actuaries (SOA) or the Casualty Actuary Society (CAS) must be completed.
  • Strong proficiency in statistical analysis.
  • Expertise in MS Excel and other programs to be utilized daily.
  • Exceptional abilities in the analytical space to analyze data, interpret trends, and make sound recommendations.
  • Savvy with programming language R in conjunction with tools like Excel to modify and analyze actuarial reports.
  • Compelling written and verbal communication skills are essential for presenting findings, collaborating with team members, and explaining complex concepts to stakeholders.
  • Detail-oriented and organized to prioritize work and time effectively.
  • Being open to growth and learning new skills is an essential piece of the mentality we cultivate in cohesion with our customers - America’s Educators!

 

Pay Range: $26/hour

  • Salary is commensurate to experience, location, etc.

Horace Mann was founded in 1945 by two Springfield, Illinois, teachers who saw a need for quality, affordable auto insurance for teachers. Since then, we’ve broadened our mission to helping all educators protect what they have today and prepare for a successful tomorrow.  And with our broadened mission has come corporate growth:  We serve more than 4,100 school districts nationwide, we’re publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange (symbol: HMN) and we have more than $12 billion in assets.

We’re motivated by the fact that educators take care of our children’s future, and we believe they deserve someone to look after theirs.  We help educators identify their financial goals and develop plans to achieve them.  This includes insurance to protect what they have today and financial products to help them prepare for their future. Our tailored offerings include special rates and benefits for educators.

EOE/Minorities/Females/Veterans/Disabled. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status

ID.me is the next-generation digital identity wallet that simplifies how individuals securely prove their identity online. Consumers can verify their identity with ID.me once and seamlessly login across websites without having to create a new login and verify their identity again. Over 175 million users experience streamlined login and identity verification with ID.me at 22 federal agencies, 50 state government agencies, and more than 100 healthcare organizations. Over 600 consumer brands use ID.me to verify communities and user segments to honor service and build more authentic relationships. ID.me’s technology meets the federal standards for consumer authentication set by the Commerce Department and is approved as a NIST 800-63-3 IAL2 / AAL2 credential service provider by the Kantara Initiative. ID.me is committed to “No Identity Left Behind” to enable all people to have a secure digital identity. To learn more, visit https://network.id.me/.

ID.me is a full-time, in-office culture. Unless a specific job description explicitly states otherwise, all roles are on-site five days per week at one of our offices in McLean, VA; Mountain View, CA; New York City, NY; or Tampa, FL. Certain roles — such as field-based sales or other remote-by-design positions — may have different work arrangements as noted in their individual postings.

At ID.me, we embrace the thoughtful use of AI tools in our daily work and there are even occasions where we leverage AI in our hiring process. ID.me is hiring a Product Security Engineering Intern for Summer 2027. You will join the Product Security team, which keeps the platform that verifies identities for over 156 million people across 21 federal agencies, 50 state agencies, and more than 600 businesses secure by design. 

This is a hands-on engineering internship, not a shadowing program. You will own a scoped project from start to finish, ship real improvements to how we build and run software, and present your results to security and engineering leadership at the end of the summer.

  • Partner with engineering teams on threat models and security design reviews for new features and services. 
  • Triage findings from static analysis (SAST), dependency scanning (SCA), secrets detection, and container scanning, and help engineers fix them. 
  • Build or improve automation that brings security checks into CI/CD pipelines and developer workflows. 
  • Help assess and improve the security posture of our cloud environments, including cloud security posture management (CSPM) and container runtime tooling. 
  • Perform focused code reviews and security testing against industry-standard and internal security frameworks and requirements. 
  • Write clear documentation, secure coding guidance, and runbooks that engineers will actually use. 
  • Deliver an intern capstone project and present it to the team at the end of the summer. 
  • Your capstone will go deep on one or two of the areas above rather than touching all of them; your mentor will help you pick the one with the clearest scope and the most direct line to a shipped improvement.

  • Familiarity with Git, the Linux command line, and basic networking concepts (HTTP, TLS, DNS). 
  • Curiosity, a builder's mindset, and the ability to explain technical risk clearly to engineers who are not security specialists. 
  • Must be authorized to work in the United States.

description:
Kensington delivers the world’s most personal travel experiences. We bring to life each client’s desire to travel in a way that’s tailored specifically for them, in the company of local private guides who ensure that they enjoy the authentic best of their destination. The result is a unique journey rich in memories that last a lifetime!

We achieve this because of our extraordinary people, passionate experts with deep knowledge of their destinations. They are what enables us to deliver remarkable experiences in over 120 countries worldwide, and across each of our businesses – Private Touring, Cruises, Villas, Yachts, Expeditions, Ultraluxe Land, Private Jets, and Air. 

To learn more about Kensington, visit kensingtontours.com. 

About the Role 

Kensington Tours is seeking a highly organized and creative Luxury Events & Content Marketing Intern to support the planning and execution of up to 8 exclusive repeat client events in 2027. This is a rare, high-impact internship at the intersection of luxury event production, influencer marketing, client relations, and multi-channel content strategy. 

This role will help bring Kensington's loyalty program to life — curating intimate, money-can't-buy experiences for our most valued repeat clients, while capturing and amplifying event content to inspire other clients and drive broader brand desire across social, email, and paid channels. 

What You'll Do

  • Client Segmentation & Invitations
  • Partner with the CRM team to segment and identify the right repeat clients for each event based on trip history, engagement, and location
  • Develop tailored event invitation copy and coordinate personalized outreach to confirmed guest lists
  • Track RSVPs, manage guest communications, and maintain accurate event attendance records 

Event Planning & Gifting 

  • Support end-to-end planning and logistics for up to 8 exclusive client events throughout 2027
  • Research, source, and coordinate procurement of custom gifts for event attendees — aligned with Kensington's luxury brand standards
  • Develop event run-of-show documents, briefing materials, and day-of logistics plans 

Influencer & Press Coordination 

  • Identify and secure one influencer and one press attendee per event — managing outreach, briefing, and attendance confirmation
  • Develop clear content briefs for influencer and press partners outlining posting expectations, key messages, and brand guidelines
  • Orchestrate on-site content capture to ensure high-quality photo and video assets are collected at each event
  • Follow up post-event to confirm influencer and press coverage is published across their respective channels 

Content Amplification & Campaign Support 

  • Work with the Integrated Marketing team to repurpose event content into social media, email, and paid campaign assets
  • Help craft post-event content narratives that generate aspirational desire among other repeat clients — positioning Kensington events as exclusive, coveted experiences
  • Track and report on content performance across channels following each event 

What We're Looking For 

  • Currently enrolled in or recently completed a degree in Event Management, Marketing, Communications, PR, or a related field
  • Demonstrated interest or experience in event planning, influencer marketing, or luxury brand environments
  • Exceptional organizational skills — able to manage multiple events and workstreams simultaneously
  • Strong written communication skills with an eye for premium, on-brand copy and messaging
  • Comfortable with outreach and relationship management — confident communicating with influencers, press contacts, and clients
  • Familiarity with social media platforms, content formats, and basic campaign reporting
  • A proactive self-starter who takes initiative and thrives in a fast-paced, creative environment
  • Passion for luxury travel, hospitality, or lifestyle brands is a strong asset 

What You'll Gain 

  • End-to-end exposure to luxury event production for a globally recognized travel brand
  • Hands-on experience with influencer and press relations in a luxury lifestyle context
  • Experience building and executing multi-channel content campaigns from real event assets
  • Direct collaboration with senior marketing, strategy, and client experience teams
  • A standout portfolio of luxury events and campaigns to showcase upon graduation 

 

Position Details:

This is a full-time, hybrid internship offering $20 per hour for 40 hours per week.

We are committed to providing employment accommodation in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code and the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act. If you require accommodation due to a disability at any stage of our hiring process, please advise us when completing your application.
